subject: Latent variable -> manifest variable => significance indices disappear?

messages.author: ab6a09a11a873aba
messages.subject: Latent variable -> manifest variable => significance indices disappear?
parts:
Hi,

Maybe this is a silly question...
I ran a model through lavaan, it ran, but I thought the amount of participants (somewhere between 200 and 300) was rather low for the amount of indicators I used. So I wanted to change a latent variable into a manifest one (this latent factor has 15 indicators at three time points). I did this and got:

Warning message:

In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :

  lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!

which seems normal because of the manifest variable, which doesn't have an error...?
When I run a summary of the results, the columns with the significance disappears. The estimates however still look like the results of the all latent factors model, but is there a way to figure out the significance level of the model with one manifest factor and all the rest stays latent?

Thanks in advance! Ellen

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: RE: Latent variable -> manifest variable => significance indices disappear?
parts:
Ellen—

     Probably, the model you specified is not statistically identified.  When identification fails (among other consequences), standard errors cannot be computed, and within standard errors, there is no way to assess “significance.”  If you will share your model syntax, I’m sure someone can spot the issue.

     You say that you changed a latent variable into a manifest variable.  How did you do that?  Common factors and observed variables are quite distinct.

     I agree that your sample size (200 < n < 300) is low for a model with at least 3 x 15 = 45 indicators.

--Ed Rigdon

messages.subject: RE: Latent variable -> manifest variable => significance indices disappear?
parts:
Ellen—

     That’s a lot of syntax, but I noticed something at the bottom.  Your R syntax concludes:

Step1 <- lavaan(SEMthreewaves, data=O)
summary(Stap1, standardized=T, fit.measures=T)

Notice that the first lines put output information into “Step1” (with an “e”) but the Summary() function references “Stap1” (with an “a”).  If this is your syntax, then it appears you are reading the wrong results.

--Ed Rigdon

parts:
Hi Ellen,

Do you still get an error if you use the "sem" function instead of the "lavaan" function?  The lavaan function has several useful defaults turned off -- it is the most flexible function, but the price of flexibility is that each parameter must be specified in your syntax OR you need to change certain defaults in lavaan() so that it behaves more like sem().  In your syntax, I notice there are latent variables with single indicators (e.g., T1V12OCCUPEXP =~ 1*T1OCCUPEXP).  You are fixing the loading to 1, but nowhere in your script do you fix the residual variance of T1OCCUPEXP to zero, which is also necessary for identification.  You can fix this either by (a) adding the appropriate parameters to the script, (b) including the argument "auto.var = TRUE" in your call to lavaan(), or perhaps most simply (c) use the sem() function instead.

I didn't study your script carefully because it is quite large :-) so I'm not sure whether there are other problems, but I would expect this to be one reason you can't get SEs.


Terry

T2V17OCCUPEXP =~ 1*T2OCCUPEXP

T2V17OCCUPEXP ~ T1V12OCCUPEXP + T1V41PEEQN
T2V40PEEN ~ T1V41PEEQN

T3V17OCCUPEXP ~ T2V17OCCUPEXP + T2V40PEEN
T3V40PEEN ~ T2V40PEEN

T1V41b1percemplextern ~~ T2V_40b_1_percemplextern + T3V_40b_1_percemplextern   
T1V41b3percemplextern ~~ T2V_40b_3_percemplextern + T3V_40b_3_percemplextern
T1V41b5percemplextern ~~ T2V_40b_5_percemplextern + T3V_40b_5_percemplextern
T1V41b7percemplextern ~~ T2V_40b_7_percemplextern + T3V_40b_7_percemplextern

T2OCCUPEXP ~~ T3OCCUPEXP
T2V_40b_1_percemplextern  ~~ T3V_40b_1_percemplextern   
T2V_40b_3_percemplextern  ~~ T3V_40b_3_percemplextern
T2V_40b_5_percemplextern  ~~ T3V_40b_5_percemplextern
T2V_40b_7_percemplextern  ~~ T3V_40b_7_percemplextern

T1OCCUPEXP ~~ T1OCCUPEXP
T1V41b1percemplextern ~~ T1V41b1percemplextern
T1V41b3percemplextern ~~ T1V41b3percemplextern
T1V41b5percemplextern ~~ T1V41b5percemplextern
T1V41b7percemplextern ~~ T1V41b7percemplextern

T2OCCUPEXP ~~ T2OCCUPEXP
T2V_40b_1_percemplextern ~~ T2V_40b_1_percemplextern
T2V_40b_3_percemplextern ~~ T2V_40b_3_percemplextern
T2V_40b_5_percemplextern ~~ T2V_40b_5_percemplextern
T2V_40b_7_percemplextern ~~ T2V_40b_7_percemplextern

T3OCCUPEXP ~~ T3OCCUPEXP
T3V_40b_1_percemplextern ~~ T3V_40b_1_percemplextern   
T3V_40b_3_percemplextern ~~ T3V_40b_3_percemplextern
T3V_40b_5_percemplextern ~~ T3V_40b_5_percemplextern
T3V_40b_7_percemplextern ~~ T3V_40b_7_percemplextern

T1V12OCCUPEXP ~~ NA*T1V12OCCUPEXP
T1V41PEEQN ~~ NA*T1V41PEEQN

T2V17OCCUPEXP ~~ NA*T2V17OCCUPEXP
T2V40PEEN ~~ NA*T2V40PEEN

T3V17OCCUPEXP ~~ NA*T3V17OCCUPEXP
T3V40PEEN ~~ NA*T3V40PEEN

T1V12OCCUPEXP ~~ T1V41PEEQN 

T2V17OCCUPEXP ~~ T2V40PEEN

T3V17OCCUPEXP ~~ T3V40PEEN 
'

Step1 <- lavaan(SEMdriewaves, auto.var = TRUE, data=O)
summary(Step1, standardized=T, fit.measures=T)
